creauit ad participandum gratiarum actione ab iis, qui noverunt veritatem. Si, inquam, manifestum sit ex testimonio Spiritus S. in Apostolo loquentes Scripturas à Deo, traditiones illas Pontificias à Diabolo inspiratas esse: ecquae tandem Antichristi vox in Ecclesia unquam agnoscetur, si haec ... [illegible, ~12 letters] Scripturas ut imperfectas accusat, perficiendas autem suis traditionibus tradat? Quid Bellarminus ad haec? Multa commentitur, quibus Apostolum eludat.

{a}Negat inde deduci, Scripturam sufficientem esse, quia vulgò dicitur, & sic deinde ratiocinatur: Si dicas, Scriptura utilis est ad hoc, sive huic habet usum, sive ad hoc refertur, & ornatur, sive quodlibet aliud simile, nunquam tamen significatur eam solam sufficere. Sicut enim, quoties cibus vitae est ad vivendum hominem, dicit quidem, cibum ad hoc esse institutum, vt nutriat, sed non dicit, sufficere solum cibum, nam si calor naturalis deficiat, aut aliquod infirmum corpus ad nutriendum nec sanum cibus non sufficit. Itaq; Apostolus non dicit, solam Scripturam sufficere ad doctrinam, argumentum, &c. & prorsus ad hominem perficiendum & absolvendum, sed tantum ad haec omnia profuisse & iuuare. Haec ille.

page.notes: Notes on the transcription: The page is heavily damaged by a dark blotch across the centre and right of the text block, and by a light spot in the centre. Many words in the blotch are uncertain and are marked [?] or illegible; the blotch extends most over the lines beginning "creauit", "Negat", "Sicut", "Itaq" and "Credo". The left-page column is cut off at the scan edge, so only word ends are visible. The page number "33" is uncertain; the digit may be 37. The marginal note marked "a" reads "lib. 4. cap. 10. de verb." (the letter "a" is the mark beside "Negat"). A second right-margin note, "Dei non script.", is printed beside the same stretch of text but has no visible reference mark, so it is not linked to a mark in the text. The last line of text ends with a printed hyphen ("cuen-"); the word continues on the next page.
